modules.title: Wave Particle Duality
modules.scope: Covered fully against the syllabus line. The photoelectric effect, Davisson-Germer experiment and uncertainty principle are not in the syllabus line but are in your decks, so they are included and marked as extra.
modules.syllabus: Dual nature of radiation – Young's double slit experiment – Blackbody radiation – Planck's hypothesis – de Broglie hypothesis – Wavefunction – Stern-Gerlach experiment.

topics.title: Dual nature of radiation and Young's double slit
topics.summary: Light shows interference (wave) yet comes in quanta (particle); Young's experiment is the wave evidence.

subtopics.title: Dual nature of radiation and matter
subtopics.summary: Wave and particle descriptions, linked by E = hν and λ = h/p.

subtopics.title: Wave characteristics and the travelling wave
subtopics.summary: λ, k, f, T, v = fλ and y = A cos(ωt − kx).

subtopics.title: Superposition and interference
subtopics.summary: Waves add; in phase doubles the amplitude, in antiphase cancels.

subtopics.title: Young's double-slit experiment
subtopics.summary: Fringes at y = nλD/d; fringe width β = λD/d.

topics.title: Blackbody radiation
topics.summary: The glow of a hot body, its laws, and the failure of classical theory.

subtopics.title: Thermal radiation, the blackbody and Kirchhoff's law
subtopics.summary: An ideal absorber is an ideal emitter.

subtopics.title: Features of the spectrum: Stefan's and Wien's laws
subtopics.summary: R = σT⁴ and λ_max T = 2.898×10⁻³ m·K.

subtopics.title: Rayleigh-Jeans law and the ultraviolet catastrophe
subtopics.summary: The classical curve diverges at short wavelength.

topics.title: Planck's hypothesis
topics.summary: Oscillator energies come in steps of hν; this gives the radiation law that fits the data.

subtopics.title: Quantisation of oscillator energy
subtopics.summary: Eₙ = nhν, quanta E = hν.

subtopics.title: Planck's radiation law and its limits
subtopics.summary: Reduces to Rayleigh-Jeans at low ν and vanishes at high ν.

topics.title: The photoelectric effect (extra: in your decks, not in the syllabus line)
topics.summary: Evidence for photons; Einstein's equation hf = W₀ + KE_max.

subtopics.title: Observations and the laws of photoelectric emission
subtopics.summary: Threshold frequency, stopping potential, instantaneous emission.

subtopics.title: Einstein's photoelectric equation
subtopics.summary: Photon energy splits into work function and kinetic energy.

topics.title: The de Broglie hypothesis and matter waves
topics.summary: Particles have wavelength λ = h/p; wave packets, phase and group velocity.

subtopics.title: De Broglie wavelength
subtopics.summary: Forms for kinetic energy, accelerating voltage and temperature.

subtopics.title: Properties of matter waves
subtopics.summary: Not electromagnetic, independent of charge, probability waves.

subtopics.title: Wave packets, phase velocity and group velocity
subtopics.summary: v_g = v and v_p = c²/v for de Broglie waves.

subtopics.title: The Davisson-Germer experiment (extra)
subtopics.summary: Electrons diffract from a crystal.

topics.title: The Heisenberg uncertainty principle (extra: in your decks, not in the syllabus line)
topics.summary: Position and momentum cannot both be sharp: Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2.

subtopics.title: Statement of the principle
subtopics.summary: Δx Δp ≥ h/4π and ΔE Δt ≥ h/4π.

subtopics.title: The microscope thought experiment
subtopics.summary: Short-wavelength photon: good position, big kick.

subtopics.title: Energy-time uncertainty and applications
subtopics.summary: Zero-point energy, line width and others.

topics.title: The wavefunction
topics.summary: The state of a particle, its probability density, acceptable forms and the operators acting on it.

subtopics.title: Meaning of the wavefunction and probability density
subtopics.summary: |Ψ|² is the probability density.

subtopics.title: Acceptable wavefunctions and normalisation
subtopics.summary: Single-valued, finite, continuous; ∫|Ψ|²dV = 1.

subtopics.title: Operators, eigenfunctions and eigenvalues
subtopics.summary: p̂ = −iħ ∂/∂x and the eigenvalue equation.

topics.title: The Stern-Gerlach experiment
topics.summary: Listed in the Module 1 syllabus; written up in full in Module 3.

subtopics.title: Where the Stern-Gerlach experiment is covered
subtopics.summary: Pointer to Module 3, Section 4.

modules.title: Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics
modules.syllabus: Introduction to linear vector space – Basis vectors – Orthonormal sets – Hilbert space – Representation of quantum states using Dirac notation – Inner and outer products – Tensor product of vector spaces – Linear operators – Matrix algebra – Hermitian, Unitary and Projection operators – Eigenvalues and eigenvectors – Pauli matrices – Commutation relations.

topics.title: Linear vector spaces
topics.summary: The arena: sets of objects you can add and scale, and how to describe them with a basis.

subtopics.title: Vector spaces and scalars
subtopics.summary: What makes a set a vector space, and why quantum mechanics needs complex scalars.

subtopics.title: Linear combinations and span
subtopics.summary: Building vectors from others; the span is everything reachable.

subtopics.title: Linear independence
subtopics.summary: No vector in the set is redundant; how to test it with a determinant or pivots.

subtopics.title: Basis vectors and dimension
subtopics.summary: A minimal complete set of vectors; coordinates depend on the basis chosen.

subtopics.title: Subspaces, column space and null space
subtopics.summary: Smaller spaces living inside a space; rank plus nullity equals the number of columns.

topics.title: Orthonormal sets and Hilbert space
topics.summary: Perpendicular unit-length bases make coordinates easy; a Hilbert space adds the inner product.

subtopics.title: Orthogonality, normalisation and orthonormal sets
subtopics.summary: Unit vectors that are mutually perpendicular; coefficients come from inner products.

subtopics.title: Hilbert space
subtopics.summary: A complete complex vector space with an inner product; where quantum states live.

topics.title: Dirac notation, inner, outer and tensor products
topics.summary: Bras, kets and the three ways of multiplying them.

subtopics.title: Kets and bras
subtopics.summary: A ket is a column vector, its bra is the conjugate transpose.

subtopics.title: Inner product
subtopics.summary: ⟨a|b⟩ gives a complex number: norm, orthogonality, Schwarz inequality.

subtopics.title: Outer product
subtopics.summary: |a⟩⟨b| gives a matrix (an operator), the reverse order of the inner product.

subtopics.title: Tensor product of vector spaces
subtopics.summary: How two spaces combine into one of dimension n×m.

topics.title: Linear operators and matrix algebra
topics.summary: Operators act on kets; in a chosen basis they are matrices. Hermitian, unitary and projection operators are the three special classes.

subtopics.title: Linear operators
subtopics.summary: Rules that map kets to kets while respecting addition and scaling.

subtopics.title: Matrix algebra and matrix representation
subtopics.summary: Matrix elements ⟨i|A|j⟩, products, transpose, dagger, trace.

subtopics.title: Hermitian operators
subtopics.summary: A = A†: real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors, the observables.

subtopics.title: Unitary operators
subtopics.summary: U†U = I: preserve norms; time evolution and gates.

subtopics.title: Projection operators
subtopics.summary: P = P† = P²: pick out a component; the tool for measurement probabilities.

topics.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
topics.summary: The directions an operator leaves unchanged, and the factors it stretches them by.

subtopics.title: The eigenvalue equation and how to solve it
subtopics.summary: Characteristic equation, then substitute back to find the vectors.

subtopics.title: Eigenvalues of Hermitian and unitary operators, and expansion in an eigenbasis
subtopics.summary: Real versus unit-modulus eigenvalues; expanding a state in eigenvectors.

topics.title: Pauli matrices
topics.summary: Three 2×2 matrices that describe spin-½ and act as qubit gates.

subtopics.title: The three Pauli matrices and their properties
subtopics.summary: σx, σy, σz: Hermitian, unitary, traceless, eigenvalues ±1.

subtopics.title: Pauli eigenstates and products
subtopics.summary: Eigenvectors of each matrix and the multiplication rules.

topics.title: Commutation relations
topics.summary: Whether the order of two operators matters, and what that means physically.

subtopics.title: Commutators, anticommutators and identities
subtopics.summary: [A,B] = AB − BA, and the rules for manipulating it.

subtopics.title: Key commutators and their physical meaning
subtopics.summary: [x,p] = iħ, angular momentum, Pauli; commuting means simultaneously measurable.

modules.title: Postulates of Quantum Mechanics
modules.scope: Covered fully, including the time-dependent and time-independent Schrödinger equations.
modules.syllabus: Observables – Expectation values – Measurement in Quantum Mechanics – Sequential Stern-Gerlach Experiment – Time-dependent and time-independent Schrödinger equations.

topics.title: Observables and operators
topics.summary: Every measurable quantity is a Hermitian operator; its eigenvalues are the possible results.

subtopics.title: What an observable is
subtopics.summary: Measurable property represented by a Hermitian operator, so results are real.

subtopics.title: The standard operators
subtopics.summary: Position, momentum, angular momentum, kinetic, potential and total energy operators.

subtopics.title: Where the momentum and energy operators come from
subtopics.summary: Differentiate a free-particle wave to read them off.

subtopics.title: The eigenvalue postulate and quantised results
subtopics.summary: Only eigenvalues are ever observed, so measured values can be discrete.

topics.title: Expectation values
topics.summary: The probability-weighted average of many identical measurements.

subtopics.title: Meaning of an expectation value
subtopics.summary: An ensemble average, not necessarily a value you will see.

subtopics.title: Computing ⟨x⟩, ⟨p⟩ and ⟨E⟩
subtopics.summary: Sandwich the operator between ψ* and ψ and integrate.

subtopics.title: Shortcuts for real wavefunctions and ⟨p²⟩
subtopics.summary: ⟨p⟩ = 0 for real ψ; ⟨p²⟩ = ħ²∫|ψ′|²dx.

subtopics.title: Uncertainty from expectation values
subtopics.summary: Δx and Δp from ⟨x²⟩ − ⟨x⟩² and checking the uncertainty principle.

topics.title: Measurement in quantum mechanics
topics.summary: Outcomes are eigenvalues, probabilities come from projections, and the state collapses.

subtopics.title: Possible outcomes and definite states
subtopics.summary: Eigenvalues are outcomes; eigenvectors are states with a certain outcome.

subtopics.title: Probabilities from projection operators
subtopics.summary: Prob = ‖Pψ‖² = |⟨a|ψ⟩|² for a normalised state.

subtopics.title: Collapse and repeated measurement
subtopics.summary: After a measurement the state is the eigenvector found; repeating gives the same result.

topics.title: Sequential Stern-Gerlach experiment
topics.summary: Chains of spin analysers reveal superposition, incompatibility and interference.

subtopics.title: The Stern-Gerlach apparatus and spin-½
subtopics.summary: A beam splits into two; kets label the beams.

subtopics.title: Experiment 1: z then z
subtopics.summary: A repeated identical measurement agrees with itself.

subtopics.title: Experiment 2: z then x
subtopics.summary: A 50/50 split: the state |+⟩ is a superposition of x-states.

subtopics.title: Experiment 3: z, x, then z
subtopics.summary: The x measurement erases the earlier z result: incompatible observables.

subtopics.title: Experiment 4: recombined beams
subtopics.summary: Adding amplitudes (not probabilities) restores the z result.

subtopics.title: Summary and the maths behind all four
subtopics.summary: Amplitude calculations that reproduce every count.

topics.title: Time-dependent and time-independent Schrödinger equations
topics.summary: The wave equation of matter: how it is built from de Broglie's idea, and its two forms.

subtopics.title: Why a wave equation, and its assumptions
subtopics.summary: Classical mechanics fails for atoms, so Schrödinger gives matter a wave function Ψ.

subtopics.title: From the classical wave equation to a plane-wave starting point
subtopics.summary: Start from ∇²Ψ = (1/v²)∂²Ψ/∂t² with Ψ = Ψ₀e^{−iωt}.

subtopics.title: The time-independent equation
subtopics.summary: Put in λ = h/mv and E = V + ½mv² to get ∇²ψ + (2m/ħ²)(E − V)ψ = 0, i.e. Ĥψ = Eψ.

subtopics.title: The time-dependent equation
subtopics.summary: Eliminate E using E = ħω to get iħ ∂Ψ/∂t = ĤΨ.

subtopics.title: Hamiltonian, stationary states and how the two forms connect
subtopics.summary: Ψ = ψ(x)e^{−iEt/ħ}: the time factor only changes the phase.

modules.title: Applications of Quantum Mechanics
modules.scope: Covered fully: the 1D box, its 3D extension, degeneracy, and quantum tunnelling.
modules.syllabus: Particle in a one-dimensional potential well – Extension to three-dimensional potential wells – Energy eigenvalues and eigenfunctions – Degeneracy of energy levels – Quantum tunneling phenomenon – Tunneling probability

topics.title: The particle in a 1D box
topics.summary: An infinite square well: the simplest system that shows quantisation.

subtopics.title: The setup: classical versus quantum
subtopics.summary: V = 0 inside, V = ∞ outside; what changes when the particle is a wave.

subtopics.title: The equation inside the box
subtopics.summary: ψ″ = −k²ψ with k² = 2mE/ħ², whose solutions are sines and cosines.

subtopics.title: Boundary conditions and the wavefunction
subtopics.summary: ψ(0) = ψ(L) = 0 forces B = 0 and kL = nπ.

subtopics.title: Energy eigenvalues
subtopics.summary: Eₙ = n²h²/(8mL²): quantised and growing as n².

subtopics.title: Normalisation and the eigenfunctions
subtopics.summary: A = √(2/L), so ψₙ = √(2/L) sin(nπx/L).

topics.title: What the solution tells us
topics.summary: Reading physics from Eₙ and ψₙ.

subtopics.title: Quantisation, spacing and the quantum number
subtopics.summary: Levels are discrete and not equally spaced.

subtopics.title: Zero-point energy
subtopics.summary: n = 0 is impossible; confinement forces a minimum energy.

subtopics.title: Nodes, antinodes and probability density
subtopics.summary: |ψₙ|² has n − 1 interior nodes; probability is not uniform.

subtopics.title: Probability in a region and the correspondence principle
subtopics.summary: Integrate |ψ|² over an interval; large n looks classical.

subtopics.title: The standing-wave (de Broglie) picture
subtopics.summary: L = nλ/2 gives the same energies.

topics.title: Extension to two and three dimensions
topics.summary: Separate the variables: the wavefunction is a product and the energies add.

subtopics.title: Separation of variables in a box
subtopics.summary: ψ = X(x)Y(y)Z(z) and E = Eₓ + E_y + E_z.

subtopics.title: Energy eigenvalues and eigenfunctions in 3D
subtopics.summary: Three quantum numbers, product of sines.

subtopics.title: Normalisation and probability in a 3D box
subtopics.summary: C = (2/L)^{3/2}; the probability in a slab is a product of three 1D integrals.

topics.title: Degeneracy of energy levels
topics.summary: Different states sharing one energy, and why a symmetric box has so many.

subtopics.title: What degeneracy means
subtopics.summary: Several wavefunctions with one eigenvalue; the number of them is the degree.

subtopics.title: Counting the levels of a cubical box
subtopics.summary: List (nₓ,n_y,n_z) with the same n² sum; permutations give the degree.

subtopics.title: Symmetry and breaking the degeneracy
subtopics.summary: Unequal sides split a degenerate level into separate ones.

topics.title: Quantum tunnelling and tunnelling probability
topics.summary: A particle can get through a barrier that classical mechanics says it cannot cross.

subtopics.title: Classical versus quantum behaviour at a barrier
subtopics.summary: Classically E < V₀ means total reflection; quantum mechanically a small part gets through.

subtopics.title: The barrier problem: regions, wave numbers and solutions
subtopics.summary: Three regions, k₁ = k₃ outside and a different k inside.

subtopics.title: Reflection and transmission probabilities
subtopics.summary: R = B*B/A*A, T = F*F/A*A, and R + T = 1.

subtopics.title: The wavefunction inside the barrier (E < V₀)
subtopics.summary: Real exponentials Ce^{κx} + De^{−κx}: it decays but does not vanish.

subtopics.title: Tunnelling probability
subtopics.summary: T ≈ 16(E/V₀)(1 − E/V₀)e^{−2κL}, or roughly e^{−2κL}.

subtopics.title: Analogy with wave optics
subtopics.summary: Frustrated total internal reflection between two prisms.

subtopics.title: Scanning tunnelling microscope
subtopics.summary: Tunnelling current depends exponentially on tip-surface distance.

subtopics.title: Alpha-particle decay
subtopics.summary: An alpha particle tunnels out through the Coulomb barrier of the nucleus.

subtopics.title: Other tunnelling phenomena
subtopics.summary: Tunnel diode, field emission, electrical breakdown of insulators.

modules.title: Elements of Quantum Computing
modules.scope: Covered fully against the syllabus line. S and T gates, SWAP, controlled-Z and Toffoli are only briefly covered because your deck marks them as not in the syllabus.
modules.syllabus: Introduction to qubits – Single qubit states and the Bloch Sphere – Two-qubit systems – Quantum entanglement and Bell states – Single-qubit gates: Pauli and Hadamard – Two-qubit gates: CNOT – Generation of entangled states.

topics.title: Qubits: from the bit to the quantum bit
topics.summary: What a qubit is, how it is written as a vector, and what superposition and measurement mean.

subtopics.title: Classical bit versus qubit
subtopics.summary: A bit is 0 or 1; a qubit is a normalised superposition and gives one outcome on measurement.

subtopics.title: The qubit as a vector in Hilbert space
subtopics.summary: |0⟩ and |1⟩ as the columns (1,0) and (0,1); a general state (α, β).

subtopics.title: Superposition, amplitudes and measurement
subtopics.summary: P(0) = |α|², P(1) = |β|², and the state collapses on measurement.

subtopics.title: Entanglement: a first look
subtopics.summary: Qubits whose joint state cannot be split into separate states.

topics.title: The Bloch sphere
topics.summary: Every single-qubit state is a point on a sphere with |0⟩ and |1⟩ at the poles.

subtopics.title: What the Bloch sphere is
subtopics.summary: Poles are |0⟩ and |1⟩; gates are rotations of the state vector.

subtopics.title: Coordinates, the state formula and special points
subtopics.summary: |ψ⟩ = cos(θ/2)|0⟩ + e^{iφ} sin(θ/2)|1⟩ and the Bloch vector.

topics.title: Two-qubit systems
topics.summary: Two qubits live in a 4-dimensional space built with the tensor product.

subtopics.title: The tensor product and the computational basis
subtopics.summary: |00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, |11⟩ as 4-component columns; n qubits need 2ⁿ amplitudes.

subtopics.title: General two-qubit state and measurement probabilities
subtopics.summary: Four amplitudes, P(ij) = |αᵢⱼ|², and collapse of one qubit.

subtopics.title: Notation: shorthand, encoded form and the x basis
subtopics.summary: |01⟩ = |0⟩|1⟩ = |1⟩², and the |±⟩ product basis.

topics.title: Entanglement and Bell states
topics.summary: Which two-qubit states are entangled, the four maximally entangled Bell states, and their uses.

subtopics.title: Product states versus entangled states
subtopics.summary: A product state has α₀₀α₁₁ = α₀₁α₁₀; failing this means entangled.

subtopics.title: Correlations, applications and experiments
subtopics.summary: Teleportation, QKD, superdense coding, error correction; Bell-inequality tests.

topics.title: Single-qubit quantum gates
topics.summary: Unitary, reversible operations on one qubit: X, Y, Z and H.

subtopics.title: What a quantum gate is: unitary and reversible
subtopics.summary: U†U = I preserves probability; contrast with irreversible AND.

subtopics.title: Pauli-X gate (the quantum NOT)
subtopics.summary: Swaps the amplitudes of |0⟩ and |1⟩.

subtopics.title: Pauli-Y gate
subtopics.summary: A flip with phases: Y|0⟩ = i|1⟩, Y|1⟩ = −i|0⟩.

subtopics.title: Pauli-Z gate (phase flip)
subtopics.summary: Leaves |0⟩, sends |1⟩ to −|1⟩.

subtopics.title: Hadamard gate
subtopics.summary: Turns basis states into equal superpositions; H² = I.

subtopics.title: Gates as rotations on the Bloch sphere
subtopics.summary: X, Y, Z are π rotations; H takes the pole to the equator.

topics.title: Two-qubit gates and generating entanglement
topics.summary: CNOT, its matrix, and the H + CNOT circuit that makes a Bell state.

subtopics.title: The CNOT gate
subtopics.summary: Flips the target when the control is |1⟩.

subtopics.title: The CNOT matrix and a matrix calculation
subtopics.summary: 4×4 permutation matrix; worked as CNOT|10⟩ = |11⟩.

subtopics.title: Creating entanglement: H then CNOT
subtopics.summary: |00⟩ → (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2, with all four Bell states from the four inputs.

subtopics.title: Other multi-qubit gates (for information)
subtopics.summary: SWAP, controlled-Z and Toffoli; not in your deck's syllabus.
